The Mother of God, Helper in Childbirth

Icons

Theotokos

The Mother of God, Helper in Childbirth

Pomozhenie Rodam · Helper of Mothers

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Luke 1:31–35

King James Version · Scripture previews

Sretensky Monastery’s published article describes this Marian type and the veneration of a particular image at Saint Nicholas the White Cathedral in Serpukhov.

[1] Published source,paragraph 12; Published source,paragraph 17

What is depicted

This nineteenth-century icon shows Mary with the infant Christ before her body. The old painted surface and losses remain visible. Its file-level title identifies the Helper in Childbirth; it is not replaced with a different image merely because both concern maternity.

[2] Exact file record File:Pomozhenie rodam.jpg,field title; Exact file record File:Pomozhenie rodam.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.ImageDescription; Exact file record File:Pomozhenie rodam.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.DateTimeOriginal; Exact file record File:Pomozhenie rodam.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Artist; Exact file record File:Pomozhenie rodam.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Credit; Exact file record File:Pomozhenie rodam.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.LicenseShortName

History and tradition

The article follows a local image’s recovery and the cathedral’s later history. It distinguishes accounts of different forms and reports help attributed to the Mother of God by people who venerated the image. Those reports remain the publication’s devotional testimony; the profile does not make promises about pregnancy or childbirth.

[1] Published source,paragraph 8; Published source,paragraph 12; Published source,paragraph 14; Published source,paragraph 15; Published source,paragraph 16; Published source,paragraph 17; Published source,paragraph 18; Published source,paragraph 22; Published source,paragraph 26

Published explanation

And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.

He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:

And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.

Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?

And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

The Gospel’s account of the conception of Christ; not a new prayer, a medical claim, or a prescribed action before this icon.

[3] Luke 1:31–35
